units.summary: Adds the package-level errorCacheTTL (5 minutes), which controls how long GetRecord keeps returning a stored failure. The comment justifies it with permanently forbidden records, but GetRecord caches every kind of error, not just those.
units.headline: New 5-minute TTL for cached record-lookup failures
units.reason: The TTL sets how long lookups are suppressed after any failure, including transient ones.
focus: Whether 5 minutes is acceptable for transient outages, given that all errors get cached (see GetRecord)

units.summary: New unexported struct that pairs an error with its expiry time. It is used only by the Client.errors map. On its own it adds no behavior; GetRecord's use of it is reviewed there.
units.headline: Add cachedError struct holding an error and its expiry
units.reason: Plain unexported data holder; the behavior lives in GetRecord.

units.summary: Client gets an errors map plus injectable get/now funcs for tests. All new fields are unexported and never serialized. The errors map, like the existing cache map, has no lock and is touched from Track outside the Loader mutex, a race that already existed before this PR.

issues.title: Client maps accessed without synchronization
issues.failure_scenario: If Loader.Track runs from two goroutines, both call loadMetadata→GetRecord with no lock, so concurrent writes to c.cache/c.errors can make Go abort with 'concurrent map writes'.

units.headline: Client gains an error cache and injectable get/now hooks
units.reason: Struct fields added that change lookup behavior; they are unexported, so wire output is unaffected.
focus: Whether Track/GetRecord can run concurrently; the errors map adds a second unlocked map

units.summary: NewClient now initializes the errors map, sets now to time.Now and points get at fetchFromServer. Production behavior depends on that wiring being correct, and it is.
units.headline: NewClient wires the error cache, clock and fetchFromServer
units.reason: Constructor wiring decides which fetch path production uses.
focus: get is bound to fetchFromServer, so production does not use a test stub

units.summary: Drops the retry parameter. Any error from get is now stored per key for errorCacheTTL and returned until it expires. That includes dial failures, timeouts and connection resets, not just FORBIDDEN replies. Because loadMetadata now discards the error, items are tracked silently without an owner.

issues.title: Transient network errors are cached for 5 minutes
issues.failure_scenario: The inventory server is unreachable for one second, so connect() returns 'failed to connect' (or the 1s request deadline expires). Every key looked up in that window is then answered from the error cache for 5 minutes without contacting the server. loadMetadata swallows the error, so those items are tracked with an empty Owner and never refreshed.

issues.title: Comment rationale doesn't match the caching scope
issues.evidence:
// Some records are permanently forbidden to this service, so asking
// on every Track call only burns connections.
issues.failure_scenario: The comment justifies caching only for permanently forbidden records, but GetRecord caches errors that are not ReplyErrors (e.g. context.DeadlineExceeded) just the same.

units.headline: GetRecord caches every lookup failure per key for errorCacheTTL
units.reason: Changes error handling and retry semantics for every inventory lookup.
focus: Whether only isErrorReply errors should be cached, not dial or timeout errors
Interaction with loadMetadata swallowing the error: items lose owner info for up to 5 minutes
errors map grows without bound for failing keys that are never looked up again

units.summary: Replaces the recursive retry with a loop. On a non-reply error it closes the connection and tries once more; on a ReplyError it returns right away. The behavior matches the old retry=true path, except server error replies are no longer retried.
units.headline: Fetch reconnects once on transport errors, never on error replies
units.reason: Retry/reconnect logic for network calls changed.
focus: After a failure on the second attempt the conn is left open; next call's first attempt must recover (same as before)
The retry reuses the original ctx, so once a deadline has expired the second attempt fails at once

units.summary: Uses errors.As to report whether err is or wraps a ReplyError. Conn.Get returns ReplyError by value, so the value target matches. Unit tests cover the bare and wrapped cases.
units.headline: Add isErrorReply to detect ReplyError via errors.As
units.reason: Small helper that is correct for the value-typed ReplyError that Conn.Get returns.

units.summary: Updates the call for the new GetRecord signature with the retry argument removed. Retrying now happens inside fetchFromServer, so the effective behavior is unchanged apart from the GetRecord changes reviewed above.
units.headline: getRecord call updated for GetRecord's new signature
units.reason: Mechanical call-site update; behavior differences come from GetRecord itself.
